See dependencyCandidates. name: approval_limit_currency_window

Relabelled to the graph's parenthesised descriptive convention. Name, quote, sourceFile, fieldType, validValues and fromRawHtmlTable stand exactly as extracted. name: approval_limit_amount
label: Amount
sourceQuote: You can enter 0 in the Amount field.
notes: BRANCH B, right side of the window; the second control in the unnamed 'Approval Limit area'. NEVER the same field record as field.workflows.authorized-approver-approval-limit (labeled 'Approval Limit', from authorized-approver-list-a9522ec8.md, Workflows-path only) — this window's own control is explicitly labeled 'the Amount field', a different label on a different surface writing the same underlying per-approver value (three-setter verdict, see step-4-assign-the-proper-rights-to-users-86389a18.md). VALUE SEMANTICS: 0 = "This puts the approver into the authorized approver workflow but will prevent that approver from having final authority to approve the invoice. They can approve the invoice to move it forward in the workflow but, since the Limit Approved status is not changed, the invoice moves to the next authorized approver or processor – depending on how the workflow is designed." (fcfd570c, the Amount-field paragraph, grep -F -c = 1). REPAIR (refuter 1, cross-branch quote splice): the extraction attributed branch A's wording to this branch-B control by including the parenthetical "(cannot limit-approve)", which occurs EXACTLY ONCE in fcfd570c and only in the branch-A Manager Approval Limit paragraph; the branch-B Amount paragraph reads "...final authority to approve the invoice. They can approve..." with no parenthetical. The parenthetical has been removed here and is carried, correctly attributed, on manager_approval_limit. This matters beyond punctuation: the splice silently erased the different-label/different-branch distinction that is the justification for emitting both records. NULL/blank = unlimited, stated here as ONE act: 'For an unlimited approval amount, leave blank (null).' (8b167b96) — surface-agnostic corroboration in setting-an-unlimited-approval-amount-9d98b489.md: 'a limit amount of null will result in an unlimited approval/no limit approval amount.' CONTRADICTION 3: Workflows/a9522ec8 requires a TWO-ACT unlimited recipe ('set to no approval limit currency, and leave the approval limit amount blank'); this window and 9d98b489 each state only ONE act. Whether the currency must ALSO be cleared here is UNDETERMINED BY THE DOCUMENTATION — do not import the Workflows two-act recipe onto this window. Value domain 'Numeric' / 'Specified in the approval limit currency' is documented only on employee-import-e28f2294.md (value-domain citation only, not a page source).

name: cost_object_approval_level
label: Level
sourceQuote: For level-based cost object approval, select a level.
notes: CONTESTED EXISTENCE - THIS CONTROL'S PRESENCE ON THIS SURFACE IS FLATLY DENIED BY A SECOND FILE AND THE CONTRADICTION IS NOT RESOLVED. Read this marker before treating the record as an ordinary control: a driver must not assume a Level control will be present in this window. REPAIR (refuter 2): the contested status lived only in the middle of prose notes and could be lost in a later summarisation pass, so it is now the first statement of the record and is wired to the page's contradiction node (the "Level control contested between User Administration and Workflows" contradiction emitted by both extraction lenses, which carries aae69350's denial sentence verbatim). NOTE ON SHAPE: the built graph's configField schema has no conditional-visibility or contested key (censused across all 607 built fields: id, pageId, name, label, fieldType, validValues, sourceQuote, sourceFile, notes, uiVariant, sourceGroup, plus fromRawHtmlTable on 6), so inventing one here would be schema invention; the marker is therefore carried at the head of notes plus the contradiction edge. REPAIR (refuter 2, added corroboration not in the brief): step-4-assign-the-proper-rights-to-users-86389a18.md - the very topic that supplies the decisive three-setter sentence - routes ALL level assignment away from this surface: "If you are assigning "levels" to authorized approvers, refer to Filter Authorized Approvers by Workflow Approval Step in this guide." (grep -F -c = 1). Recorded as STRENGTHENING the two-values-one-label hypothesis for the AUTHORIZED-APPROVER level, explicitly NOT as a resolution: 86389a18 and aae69350 are both in the Authorized Approvers guide thread, while 8b167b96 is in the Cost Object Approval thread and was never in dialogue with them. REPAIR (refuter 2, label collision stated rather than assumed): the label "Level" already means four different things in the built graph - field.feature-hierarchies.level, field.workflows.authorized-approver-level, field.accounting-administration.segment-level and field.purchase-order-matching-rules.level-field. This record is a FIFTH, distinct control and its name is deliberately cost_object_approval_level so no reader can mistake it for a sibling of field.workflows.authorized-approver-level (whose own sourceQuote, "The Level field appears if levels have been assigned to a workflow approval step.", shows it to be the workflow-step filter). BRANCH B, right side of the window, CONTESTED. 8b167b96 documents this control on the window; filter-authorized-approvers-by-workflow-approval-step-aae69350.md states the flat opposite: 'Levels cannot be added to approvers via User Administration.' and 'The levels can be added to users via the Employee Import or the Authorized Approver list (Administration > Invoice > Workflows > Authorized Approver tab).' Both grep -F verify; see contradictions[] — NOT RESOLVED, recorded as a hypothesis only. HYPOTHESIS (not adopted as fact): these are two DIFFERENT VALUES sharing one label. aae69350's 'Level' is the authorized-approver workflow-step FILTER (employee import record TYPE 720 per step-2-assign-the-level-to-the-approver-d8bf669c.md — 'authorized approvers may be assigned to levels via record type 720 in the employee import' — feeding the Authorized Approver Hierarchy), while 8b167b96's 'Level' is the level-based COST OBJECT APPROVAL level (employee import record SET 710 per employee-import-e28f2294.md, feeding a separately-named Cost Object Approver Hierarchy per step-1-define-the-cost-object-approver-hierarchy-6e7b7dc6.md). Given this distinction, name it cost_object_approval_level and NEVER present it as a sibling of the built field.workflows.authorized-approver-level. STRUCTURAL CONTEXT for the contradiction: 8b167b96 belongs to the Cost Object Approval guide thread (gates on 'the Cost Object Approver feature'; rev-history root cost-object-approval-8b3d1e0f.md; Step 4 sibling step-4-assign-the-proper-rights-to-users-82481079.md; Configuration sibling configuration-8b3cce3f.md), a materially different chapter than fcfd570c's Authorized Approvers guide thread — offered as a hypothesis for why the two attestations diverge, not as a resolution. PRECEDENCE RULE (see dependencyCandidates): if BOTH the Approval Limit area and this Level field are completed, 'Concur Invoice will use the one that applies to your configuration and ignore the other' (8b167b96) — the cost object configuration (limit vs level, per level-based-approvals-and-limit-based-approvals-b335cf33.md) decides which is authoritative.
